warning_model.strategic_warning: VERY_HIGH before the raid; Marianas is already CRITICAL/PERSISTENT.
warning_model.interpretation: Branch radar/visual/plot/radio network buys readiness and dispersal. It is not US-style GCI and does not provide perfect altitude/identity/weapon-quality control.

defense_result.air_to_air_and_AA: Japanese fighter sections enter with materially better energy/readiness than historical surprise conditions, but are outnumbered by the F6F sweep and still lose the tactical air battle.
defense_result.note: Evacuated/rebased aircraft are not losses. The branch deliberately preserves attack/recon cadres rather than keeping every aircraft onsite for a doomed second interception.

base_system_end_11Jun.water_aviation_state: Dispersed and still useful; vulnerable exposed moorings are reduced before follow-on raids.
base_system_end_11Jun.repair_outlook: Some short-term unavailable aircraft/runway capacity can return overnight; do not subtract repairable losses again on 12 Jun.

offensive_response: NO COORDINATED ANTI-CARRIER STRIKE on 11 Jun. Incoming-raid bearing is not a sufficiently fresh carrier track. Yamamoto/area air command prioritizes dispersal, recon preservation and night recontact attempts over a speculative long-range strike.
shipping: High pre-raid warning starts staggered evacuation/dispersal of navigable Saipan shipping before and during 11 Jun. This reduces harbor target density but creates a moving-convoy gate for 12 Jun; do not auto-copy the historical convoy loss cluster before that adjudication.
